ms1582f2.summary: Charles V tells his ambassadors in London how to answer the French peace overtures: he has always wanted peace, the French broke the truce of their own will, his proposal of September 1553 made at the request of the Cardinal of Imola (Dandino) was never answered; he will negotiate through Mary Tudor once French terms for peace or truce are known; Renard is to learn from Paget what the French ambassador said about marriage matches.
ms1582f2.en:
Cipher passage of Charles V's letter to his ambassadors in England (Lalaing, Egmont, Courrières, Simon Renard),
Brussels, 24 January 1554. The text is already in print from the minute: Gachard, Collection des voyages des
souverains des Pays-Bas IV (1882), appendix CLV, pp. 311-314 (this passage pp. 313-314); English calendar in Tyler,
CSP Spain XII (1949), pp. 44-49 (this passage pp. 46-47). This reading is made from the cipher, decoded with the key
in key.tsv (an independent re-derivation of the cipher published by Pich-Ponce 2024), and is given so that the
cipher, the contemporary decipherment on the page and the printed minute can be compared.

Marks: sure (no mark: the decode spells the word) / {probable} (the decode is off by a sign or a key value but the
word is clear and agrees with the minute) / [restored] (not in the decode, supplied from the minute) / [...

system: Charles V's French cipher to Simon Renard, 1549-1554, as published by Pich-Ponce (2024): numbers for letters (a..t = 20..2, a second series 21-39), syllables written as the letter preceding the consonant plus a vowel mark (+ a, bar above e, bar below i, two…
